_about.kind: Original content written for this project — NOT transcribed from any published book.
_about.note: Authored jobs (src/engine/missions/*.ts) cite their source book and page. These pools do not, because there is none: they are written in the Cyberpunk RED idiom to feed the procedural generator. Never add a page citation here.
_about.slots: Templates interpolate {patron}, {org}, {district}, {target}, {fixer}, {opposition}. Every slot a template uses must exist, or the generator throws. One exception by design: an archetype's `background` is the pitch a player hears BEFORE taking the job, and must never name {patron} or {org}. Who is paying is what negotiating an offer buys (engine/negotiation.ts), and a pitch that gives it away for free makes that ask worthless.

_rules.dvs: Every dv below must be a published Difficulty Value (dv-table.json): 9, 13, 15, 17, 21, 24, 29.
_rules.skills: Every skill below must be a printed Skill name from skills.json, so the GM can map it to a real skill id.
_rules.force: Every opposition entry names a force key from data/rules/threats.json. It is READ, never drawn, so adding this field changed no existing job: the fiction of who is against you decides the statblocks of who turns up, instead of the GM model inventing them.

archetypes.title: Retrieval in {district}
archetypes.background: {fixer} passes the job along without editorial. A client they will not name wants {target} out of {district} and into their hands, quietly, before the week turns. {why} The fee is real money for a night's work, which is the part that should worry you.
archetypes.backgroundBrief: A clean-sounding retrieval. It is not clean. Establish {district} — {colour} — and let the money look better than the job.
archetypes.hookBrief: {patron} meets in person. {tell} They will not say who else is looking for {target}, only that speed matters more than subtlety. The Edgerunner is being hired because someone expendable was required.
archetypes.legworkBrief: The Edgerunner needs a way in, and {district} offers two: the people who work the site, and the site itself. Present both without steering.

approaches.label: Work a contact on the inside
approaches.brief: Someone on the payroll drinks nearby and resents management. They can be bought, charmed, or leaned on — but they will remember which one it was.

approaches.label: Case the site yourself
approaches.brief: Two hours on a facing rooftop reads the whole rhythm of the place: shift change, camera arcs, which door is propped open for a smoke break.

archetypes.complicationBrief: Word comes that {the} is already moving. It turns out {opposition} — {oppositionFlavour} — got the same job from the other side, or got there first. The window is closing tonight, not this week.

complicationChecks.note: Only if the Edgerunner gives chase by vehicle.

archetypes.climaxBrief: It comes down to a room with {the} in it and {opposition} between. Frame the geography — cover, exits, distance in metres — and let the player choose violence or something cleverer. Both are real options.
archetypes.resolutionBrief: The handoff. {patron} takes {the}, pays what was agreed, and the Edgerunner learns just enough about why to wish they hadn't. Night City keeps the change.

archetypes.title: Extraction from {district}
archetypes.objective: Get the package out of {district} alive
archetypes.background: {fixer} makes the introduction and then makes themselves scarce. The client needs a person pulled out of {district} tonight — willing or not, and the brief is deliberately vague about which. {why}
archetypes.backgroundBrief: An extraction with a soft centre: the package may not want extracting. Establish {district} — {colour} — and keep the ambiguity live.
archetypes.hookBrief: {patron} briefs fast and leaves faster. {tell} The Edgerunner gets a face, an address, and a window. Nobody mentions what happens to the package afterward.
archetypes.legworkBrief: Two ways to find the package before the window opens: the paper trail, or the people who have seen them.

approaches.label: Follow the paper trail
approaches.brief: Delivery manifests, clinic intakes, a lease under a cousin's name. Boring work that puts a pin on a map.

approaches.label: Ask around the neighbourhood
approaches.brief: People here answer questions from someone who buys a round and doesn't look like a cop. They also talk about who was asking.

archetypes.complicationBrief: The package is guarded — not by {opposition}, yet, but by people who love them. Circling the block are {opposition}, {oppositionFlavour}, and they are not here to extract anybody.
archetypes.climaxBrief: The window opens, and {opposition} move at the same moment. Give the player the package, the exit, and not enough time — and let the package have an opinion.
archetypes.resolutionBrief: Whatever crossed the district line is what {patron} pays for. Let the Edgerunner sit with the shape of what they just did, then let {org} close the file.

archetypes.title: Sabotage in {district}
archetypes.objective: Put the operation in {district} out of commission
archetypes.background: {fixer} says only that the client pays on results. Somebody with money wants something in {district} to stop working — permanently enough to matter, quietly enough to deny. {why}
archetypes.backgroundBrief: Industrial sabotage with a deniability clause. Establish {district} — {colour} — and make clear nobody will confirm this conversation happened.
archetypes.hookBrief: {patron} supplies a floor plan two revisions out of date and a hard deadline. {tell} No support, no extraction, no acknowledgement if it goes wrong.
archetypes.legworkBrief: The Edgerunner needs to know what actually breaks the place: the machinery, or the people running it.

approaches.label: Study the machinery
approaches.brief: Schematics, load ratings, and the one subsystem whose failure takes everything else with it. Elegant, if it works.

approaches.label: Work the crew
approaches.brief: A shift supervisor with gambling debts is a better tool than any charge. Riskier: people talk, and this one might.

archetypes.complicationBrief: The floor plan was wrong, or the schedule was. On site tonight, and on nobody's list, are {opposition} — {oppositionFlavour}. Improvise or walk — and walking has a price too.
archetypes.climaxBrief: The job goes loud, or it goes perfectly and then goes loud, with {opposition} between the Edgerunner and the door. State distances in metres and let the clock run.
archetypes.resolutionBrief: Something in {district} stops working. {patron} never says thank you and the payment arrives from an account with no name on it. Someone will come looking eventually.

archetypes.title: Protection detail in {district}
archetypes.objective: Keep the principal breathing until morning
archetypes.background: {fixer} calls it babysitting and does not laugh. The client needs a body between themselves and {district} for one night, and their name is not part of the briefing yet. {why} That is exactly why someone wants them dead.
archetypes.backgroundBrief: A bodyguard job where the threat is real and the principal is not being straight. Establish {district} — {colour} — and keep the night closing in.
archetypes.hookBrief: {patron} explains the schedule and omits the reason. {tell} One night, three stops, no questions — and a fee high enough to answer the questions anyway.
archetypes.legworkBrief: Before the night starts, the Edgerunner can prepare the route or read the principal. Either buys something the other doesn't.

approaches.label: Scout the route ahead
approaches.brief: Three stops, two chokepoints, one stretch with no cover at all. Knowing which is which is the whole job.

approaches.label: Read the principal
approaches.brief: What they are lying about narrows who is coming. They will not appreciate being read.

archetypes.complicationBrief: The first stop goes wrong early. Working the route are {opposition}, {oppositionFlavour}, which means someone sold the schedule — and only a few people had it.

complicationChecks.note: Only if the principal or the Edgerunner is hurt.

archetypes.climaxBrief: They come properly the second time, at the chokepoint. Frame cover and distance in metres. The principal is a liability, not an ally — play them that way.
archetypes.resolutionBrief: Dawn over {district}. If the principal is alive, {patron} pays and asks nothing. If not, the conversation is shorter. Either way the reason stays buried.

archetypes.title: Quiet inquiry in {district}
archetypes.background: {fixer} passes it on because it is beneath them and above the client's means. Somebody is paying to know what became of {target} in {district}. {why} No police, no noise, no report in writing.
archetypes.backgroundBrief: An investigation that turns out to be about somebody's exposure, not somebody's grief. Establish {district} — {colour} — and let the client's calm sit slightly wrong.
archetypes.hookBrief: {patron} is measured about it, which is itself the tell. {tell} They want an answer, and there is a clear sense they would prefer one particular answer.
archetypes.legworkBrief: Two threads: the last place {target} was seen, and the people who profited by it. Both lead somewhere; only one is safe.

approaches.label: Work the last known location
approaches.brief: A cleaned room cleaned by someone in a hurry. What is missing says more than what is left.

approaches.label: Follow who profited
approaches.brief: Shell accounts and a transfer timed a little too well. Dry work that names a person.

archetypes.complicationBrief: The answer implicates the client. Already cleaning up behind the Edgerunner, one interview at a time, are {opposition} — {oppositionFlavour} — and the Edgerunner is now on the list.
archetypes.climaxBrief: The truth and the cleanup crew arrive together, {opposition} in the room and the evidence within reach. Distances in metres — and telling the truth is as live an option as shooting.
archetypes.resolutionBrief: The Edgerunner knows what happened to {target}. What they do with it — sell it, bury it, hand it to {patron} — is the last real choice, and Night City will price it accordingly.
